title: Per-model token-rate collapse during regional burst - investigation & hotfix
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a regional traffic spike on 2026-02-28 we observed sustained drop in tokens/sec (30–70%) and elevated TTFT for a subset of medium-length chat models (4k context family) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Impacted customers reported slow streaming starts and frequent client-side timeouts. Scope analysis shows regression is per-model and per-worker affinity dependent rather than global infra saturation.

What we observed:
- Tokens/sec dropped primarily on workers that switched from model variant A->A-quantized fallback under load; other identical workers maintained expected throughput.
- First-byte time increased by 2x for affected requests; completion latency increased proportionally.
- KV cache hit rate dropped for affected workers despite identical request distribution, indicating cache eviction or mis-indexing.
- Incidents surfaced concurrently across hosted and on-prem deployments, suggesting runtime selector/kernel interaction rather than cloud control plane.

Initial triage & hypothesis:
- Hypothesis 1: Kernel selection heuristic mis-evaluates stride/sequence footprint after runtime batching change, causing suboptimal instruction paths and reduced token throughput for some model widths.
- Hypothesis 2: KV cache eviction policy has a race with new continuous-batching prefetch pipeline; some workers are thrashing the KV shard index leading to low effective cache hits.
- Hypothesis 3: Fallback to quantized model variant triggers a different kv-key layout that our cache warming code doesn't populate, producing cold-cache microbursts.

Immediate mitigations implemented:
- Rolled an emergency routing policy to bias new requests away from workers with >25% token-rate drop. This reduced customer errors by ~60% but does not address root cause.
- Temporarily disabled aggressive prefetch-on-assign in the batcher for affected pools to stop cache churn.
- Deployed a hotfix that pins kernel selection to previous stable heuristic for 4k-context models in runtime-1.20 Canary.

Data & signals we are tracking:
- Per-worker tokens/sec, TTFT p50/p95, KV hit ratio, kernel-selection histogram, quantized-variant ratio, and CPU/GPU util. Dashboards: /dashboards/ops/ttft_regional_burst and /dashboards/eng/kv_eviction_analysis.

Planned next steps:
- Short (24–72h): run targeted A/B on canary with pinned kernel selector and slower prefetch cadence; if stable, roll to affected pools with controlled ramp.
- Medium (1–2 weeks): add deterministic KV-key tracing and an end-to-end cache warmup sequence for variant fallbacks; instrument per-model cache residency metrics.
- Long (2–6 weeks): revisit kernel heuristic to include observed sequence stride distribution and model-variant transition cost; add safety check that prevents immediate variant fallback when KV-hit < threshold.

Customer comms & PRs:
- Notified affected customers via account teams (email templates prepared and sent).
- Reference PRs: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/8243 (emergency-routing), github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/8251 (pin-kernel-heuristic), github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/8270 (batcher-prefetch-disable).

Runbooks & follow ups:
- Create runbook entry "TTFT-collapse-per-model" with mitigation playbook and dashboard links.
- Schedule postmortem and root-cause writeup when confidence >90%.
- Follow-up tickets: add kv-key diagnostic traces (ENG-120412), kernel-heuristic regression tests (ENG-120418), on-prem compatibility test matrix (ENG-120420).
